children: TOKYO--Japan's exports rose for a 13th straight month in September as the artificial intelligence boom continued to support external demand.
Exports climbed 16.7% from a year earlier on the back of strong demand for electronic components and chip-making machines, according to government data released Wednesday.
That compared with August's 19.3% increase and the 20.1% rise expected in a poll of economists by data provider LSEG.
Meanwhile, imports rose 18.9% from a year earlier, compared with a 28.0% gain in August. That resulted in a trade deficit of 536.5 billion yen, equivalent to $3.39 billion.
Economists expect Japan's export growth to remain supported by solid demand for AI-related technology equipment, though geopolitical tensions continue to pose risks to the outlook.

The steady trade figures support the Bank of Japan's view that the Middle East conflict won't cause a significant downturn in the domestic economy, giving the central bank more leeway as it weighs the timing of the next interest-rate hike.
Markets are currently pricing in nearly an 80% chance of a December rate increase.
